claim: For the homogeneous optimal-control problem in Theorem 6.5 of Weng–Chitour–Mason, let \(V_\infty\) be its value function, \(K=\{x:V_\infty(x)=1\}\), and \(m=\min_{x\in K}F(x)>0\). The Lyapunov comparison rigorously gives \[T_{x_0}\leq\frac{d+\mu}{m\mu}V_\infty(x_0)^{\mu/(d+\mu)}.\] The coefficient required by this proof is the minimum of the running cost on the unit value-function level set, not its maximum; an admissible anisotropic example has distinct minimum and maximum. This corrects the displayed comparison argument and does not claim that the printed maximum-based numerical bound is false by every possible argument.

correctness.rationale: The HJB equation gives \(\dot V_\infty=-F-\frac1q|\partial_nV_\infty|^{q/(q-1)}\leq-F\). Homogeneity and \(m=\min_K F>0\) give \(F\geq mV_\infty^{d/(d+\mu)}\); integrating \(\frac{d}{dt}V_\infty^{\mu/(d+\mu)}\leq-\frac{m\mu}{d+\mu}\) proves the stated bound. The anisotropic example verifies \(\min_KF<\max_KF\) under the stated assumptions.

evidence: The source proof uses \(\dot V_\infty\leq-F\) and then defines \(c=\max_{x\in K}F(x)\) before asserting \(\dot V_\infty\leq-cV_\infty^{d/(d+\mu)}\).

The anisotropic admissible example \(F(x_1,x_2)=|x_1|^{10/7}+|x_2|^{5/3}\) shows \(\min_K F<\max_K F\): if \(F\) were constant on \(K\), homogeneity would force \(V_\infty=CF^{11/10}\), contradicting the HJB equation at \((s,0)\), \(s\ne0\).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The maximum gives an upper bound on \(F\) along a normalized level set, whereas the derivative comparison requires a lower bound. The example rules out treating the extrema as interchangeable. The result establishes the corrected minimum-based estimate and a proof gap in the displayed maximum-based argument, but does not claim the stated numerical bound is false by every possible alternative proof.
